scope: Read-only source reasoning about direct current counters + indexed due-expiry guard + completed earlier prune. Not a claim of language-level impossibility.
positiveFinding: Final-transaction reads of engine-maintained periodPosts under the current follows can eliminate stale followed-post accumulation and correctly observe deletions, for the public nonexpiring posts in that qualified fixture. Unique recipient/period receipt, log and effect in one transaction can prevent repeated nonzero logical emission. Neither establishes unread/expiry correctness.
finiteCounterexample: At t0, the earlier prune visits a relevant unread message with expiry t2>t0 and leaves it present.
The job completes that sweep, processes other recipients, then reaches this recipient at t3>t2. The final expiry guard correctly sees remaining due content.
An if guard suppresses this recipient while the chunk cursor advances; later timer cleanup never revisits the omitted recipient/period.

A require guard instead parks the chunk. Even if a subsequent finite timer turn cleans every due row, job_head excludes parked jobs. Restart preserves the parked state; explicit operator resume is required.
If the guard is removed, the earlier sweep supplies no proof that the counter excludes the now-expired contribution. This can emit an incorrect positive count.

additionalObligations.globalGuard: A global due-expiry absence guard also depends on unrelated users, non-digest content and possibly unrelated timers. Busy unrelated expiry can prevent emission; absence of due rows proves freshness only with complete, atomic counter provenance. Timer64 is not a drained proof.
additionalObligations.pruneScope: Existing published schema has no appropriate recipient/expiry counter index. Existing expiresAt is mutable; job sweep indexes require immutable fields. A legal byId/period sweep can still finish before later expirations. No ordinary earlier sweep is a final-time snapshot.
additionalObligations.counterProvenance: Schedule fixture postPeriodCounters is incremented on create but not paired with all allowed post deletions. Its purgeMessage nulls body/expiresAt without clearing periodUnread, so even an empty expiry index may coexist with stale unread counts. Combining correct engine-maintained post counts repairs that branch, not current-message eligibility.
additionalObligations.memberships: Original requirement includes1000 memberships as well as500 follows. Current membership incarnation must select the count in the final transaction. Existing schedule sample first100 is incomplete; earlier authorizing/filtering slices cannot replace final validation.
additionalObligations.oldPeriods: A parked earlier period must not be overtaken by pruning from newer completed periods. Period schedules can skip missed intervals; the persisted daily clock recipe can retain a cutoff but has no automatic same-cutoff retry of a failed eligibility guard. Pruning at ambient current time would discard still-required older buckets.
additionalObligations.zeroOnce: A nonzero unique receipt/effect transaction proves logical-once emission. It cannot turn a deferred recipient into a completed zero, nor prove correct zero suppression from stale counters. Partial work/restart must retain the same pending period and retry it automatically.

countOnlyTerm.meaning: Public count absence evidence within that closure, not the whole final transaction. The same report separately includes1000 serialized point keys/envelopes (1109000 bytes) and pooled maintained-row first images, plus other tables.

costEvidence.limitation: The exact staged0.0.29 check refuses this compact1000-membership/500-follow final fold before expiry guards. It uses a simplified schedule fixture, not full private/expiry-safe production semantics. The retained2,531,718-byte count term was not an entire admission. This does not prove every possible authored counter design must refuse.

nextDecision: This check does not justify implementing or teaching the candidate. Closing it would require a concrete affordable final counter program plus a persisted same-period retry/eligibility protocol and atomic source maintenance, then a runtime witness. That is a separately decided authored form, not a demonstrated existing qualified recipe or a ceiling/runtime change.

facts: createRecipePost increments an explicit counter; per-user final fold selects500 follows and only100 memberships; later prune covers old periods.
500-follow cap;100-membership cap; periodUnread carries no expiry provenance; explicit post counters have ordinary authored writers.
purgeMessage clears body/expiresAt without removing periodUnread; daily clock recipe owns period catch-up but no same-cutoff guard retry.
periodPosts is engine-maintained and updates with post deletion; posts have no expiry or private-author eligibility in this fixture.
Job chunks reject range/cursor/merge sweep bounds and mutable sweep-index columns; refused chunks require explicit resume.
job_head selects queued/running only; parked jobs do not automatically resume when the due queue drains.
resume_job_at changes parked to queued by explicit operator action.
A background turn fires bounded timers then runs one job chunk; jobs do not share a snapshot.
At most64 oldest due timers per turn.
Unique receipt/effect transaction and daily retained cutoff solve logical-once/catch-up only if data eligibility is established; zero output and data-maintenance obligations explicit.
